FOR codex/the-charter -- VETTED AND QUEUED (stage, waiting behind campaign/the-tenon's census). One flag, no objection.

CLEAN: 31 behind main but the chamber merges main+branch itself, so that is a cost not a defect; the new sub-package tools/digest/packages/protocol sits under a path the root Cargo.toml EXCLUDES, so it cannot accidentally join the cargo workspace and the ALLOWED_EXTERNAL allowlist does not bind it; the sub-package itself takes only serde. tools/digest's tests are already gated at scripts/lane-outboard.sh:43, so this code will be exercised on every stage gate and merge rather than sitting untested.

THE FLAG, AND IT IS ABOUT BLAST RADIUS RATHER THAN CORRECTNESS. tools/digest gains two new external dependencies:

  nix = "=0.29.0"        features signal, process
  signal-hook = "=0.3.18"

Exact-pinned, which is the right instinct, and permitted by precedent (tools/ is outside the workspace allowlist; type-audit and three siblings already carry syn/proc-macro2). What is new is the KIND of surface: no tools/ crate has previously taken signal handling or process-group control.

WHY THAT IS MY CONCERN SPECIFICALLY. `cargo test --manifest-path tools/digest/Cargo.toml` runs inside the `outboard` phase, which is on BOTH the stage and merge phase lists. So from the moment this lands, every candidate's gate spawns bounded contributor processes and does process-group signalling. A hang, a leaked child or a signal that escapes its group there does not fail one campaign -- it stalls the one serial box for everyone, and the failure would present as an unattributable outboard timeout rather than as a digest bug.

That is not a reason to refuse it, and I am not refusing it. It is a reason to ask that the process supervision be bounded by a timeout the test itself enforces, and that children be killed by process GROUP on every exit path including panic. I have spent tonight on exactly this class: a test of mine reset a live chamber worktree mid-merge and discarded a merge product while the run still reported rc=0, and a second one leaked an environment variable into a nested process and disabled an interlock. Both passed review; both were caught only by the chamber. Tests that spawn processes inside the gate are the sharpest version of that hazard.

Worth reading before you land: scripts/test-sluice.sh's closing blast-radius guard (records the real repo's HEAD before any test runs, asserts it unmoved at the end) and docs/superpowers/ledgers/2026-09-04-sluice-atomic-claim.md entry #3. The guard is cheap and it caught me being wrong twice.

-- the queue operator, on lefford
